name: slack-radar
description: A Slack triage crew that remembers, reading with your own Slack identity through your Slack MCP — no bot, no invite. Watches the channels you choose, classifies every new message as a bug report, feature request, question, already-answered or noise with a priority, links clusters to existing GitHub issues and PRs, notices when a thread looks resolved, and sends you a daily digest — keeping everything in a local ledger so nothing is triaged twice.
author: iamwhatever
highlights: Reads with your own Slack identity via your Slack MCP: no bot, no invite, nothing visible in the channel
Read-only by construction: a hard allowlist of five read tools; the only write is an optional digest DM to yourself
One crew for every channel you configure: new messages are classified by category and priority with a one-line summary
Its own per-channel cursor, independent of your Slack read state
Flags threads that look resolved for the crew to judge; code never closes an item on its own
An expired Slack MCP login shows as 'needs re-login', never as 'no new messages'
Clusters of reports are investigated by a read-only subagent that links matching GitHub issues and PRs

args: import os,runpy,sys;h=[os.environ.get('KIROCREW_HOME',''),os.path.expanduser('~/.kiro/crew'),os.path.expanduser('~/.kirocrew')];p=next((os.path.join(d,'apps','slack-radar','backend','mcp_server.py') for d in h if d and os.path.isfile(os.path.join(d,'apps','slack-radar','backend','mcp_server.py'))),None);p or sys.exit('slack-radar: mcp_server.py not found under the crew home');runpy.run_path(p,run_name='__main__')

crons.name: daily-digest
crons.message: Call the slack_radar_request_digest tool exactly once with no arguments, then stop. Do not read the ledger, do not compose anything, and produce NO other output - the Slack Radar crew composes the digest in its own session.

useCases: Triage support and feedback channels continuously with your own Slack identity, link reports to existing GitHub work, and get one daily summary instead of reading every channel.
configuration: Install and log in to a Slack MCP server on the gateway host (default command: ai-community-slack-mcp; configurable in Settings), then list the channel IDs to watch and pick a digest destination (self-DM or dashboard notification).
